title: transient-load-shear-gateway-and-slo-trickle-stop
author: Aisha Kumar
description: Motivation: Production incidents showed correlated tenant spikes causing regional SLO thrashing when backend KV pressure and bursty fastpath requests coincide. This PR introduces a transient "load-shear gateway" that applies a soft, SLO-aware shedding curve for non-critical routes and a timeboxed "trickle-stop" mode for tenant cohorts when regional error/latency budgets are exhausted. The change is intentionally conservative: it never blocks high-priority customers, prefers shed decisions by route metadata and token-bucket scoring, and integrates with existing circuit state so we avoid double-enforcement. Changes include: 1) admission/gateway layer that computes a dynamic shear score combining region_slo_headroom, kv_pressure, and inflight_fastpath_ratio; 2) a thin token-bucket-based trickle-stop that paces retries and gracefully queues low-priority requests with a capped window (50ms per request additional latency budget by default); 3) integration points to the circuit-breaker state machine so shear is relaxed when circuits are open for lower-latency fallbacks; 4) Prometheus metrics and tracing spans for visibility; 5) a short rollback path and feature-flag gating for staged rollout. Test plan: unit tests for scoring logic, integration test harness simulating KV pressure + tenant spike, chaos run in perf-canary region, and a 48-hour canary with traffic shaping. Rollout plan: enable in perf-canary for 24h, staged ramp in us-west-2 and eu-west-1, enable global after 48h when error budgets stabilize. Rollback: flip feature flag or revert head branch; token-bucket state is ephemeral and drains within 60s. Related: Linear ENG-7261 tracks follow-ups (fine-tune thresholds per customer cohort); incident ref SUP-411 triggered this change.
commits_summary: Add transient load-shear gateway module with scoring and admission APIs
Implement token-bucket trickle-stop and per-route priority classification
Wire shear decisions into circuit-breaker state machine (relax-on-open)
Add integration tests simulating kv pressure and tenant spike
Feature flag and rollout config; docs and release note draft
review_thread: Mateo Rivera: Can we avoid interacting with the existing admission quota? Suggest adding a clear precedence doc - resolved by adding precedence table and tests.
Liang Chen: Scoring formula looks reasonable but thresholds should be configurable per-region. Added region config map and runtime flags.
Sara O'Neill: Request more telemetry around 'relax_on_circuit_open' - added counter and trace tag to show when relaxation happens.
Aisha Kumar: Addressed feedback: added precedence table, region config, extra metric, and tightened default thresholds. PTAL.
Liang Chen: Approve after CI green.
Mateo Rivera: Approve - minor nits fixed.
release_notes: Introduce a conservative, feature-flagged regional load-shear gateway and token-bucket based trickle-stop to reduce correlated SLO violations during KV pressure spikes. Metrics and rollout instructions included. No breaking changes; gated behind feature flag and staged rollout.
merge_commit_message: squash: introduce transient load-shear gateway and trickle-stop (ENG-7261) - A. Kumar
observability_notes: New metrics: redwood_load_shear_score{region,route}, redwood_trickle_stop_active{region}, redwood_trickle_stop_shed_count_total. Tracing spans: load_shear.evaluate and load_shear.enforce. Alerting: add a temporary SLI to detect >5% shed rate in canary region.
operational_impact: When enabled, low-priority routes may see increased 429/503 backpressure during regional high-pressure windows; high-priority routes are exempt. Expected reduction in regional tail latency and error amplification. Token-bucket state is ephemeral and resets on process restart.
rollback_instructions: Flip feature flag 'load_shear.gateway.enabled' to false in Console or revert the deployment. Token buckets drain within configured window (default 60s). If rollback fails, scale down new deploy and revert to previous release tag.
notes_for_oncall: If canary shows >2% customer-visible error increase for high-priority routes, roll back immediately. Observe metrics prefixed with redwood_trickle_stop_ and trace any requests with tag load_shear=1. Contact author Aisha Kumar or SRE pager for escalations.
diff_examples:
+ func evaluateScore(region string, stats RegionStats) float64 { // new composite score combining slo, kv pressure, inflight
+    score := 0.0
+    score += clamp(1 - stats.SLOHeadroom, 0, 1) * 0.6
+    score += clamp(stats.KVPressure, 0, 1) * 0.3
+    score += clamp(stats.InflightFastpathRatio, 0, 1) * 0.1
+    return score
+}
+ type TrickleBucket struct { lastTick int64; tokens float64 } // simple per-tenant pacing bucket
